record.paper_title: Open problems, questions and challenges in finite-dimensional integrable systems
record.original_question: Consider the action of Aut(V, J ) on V. Describe the partition of V into Aut(V, J )- orbits. More generally, describe the action of Aut(V, J ) on the set of all k-dimensional subspaces U ⊂ V (orbits, invariants, fixed points). Notice that fixed points of this action (i.e., Aut(V, J )- invariant subspaces) are important, as they correspond to w ell-defined (co)distributions in the context of Poisson pencils. A subspace L ⊂ V is said to be bi-Lagrangian if it is simultaneously isotropic with respect to both A and B and has maximal possible dimension (which is 1 2 (dim V + corank J)). The set LG( V, J ) of all bi-Lagrangian subspaces is called the bi-Lagrangian Grassmannian. A detailed description of 24 LG(V, J ) is an important open problem, see the discussion in [195]. It is importa nt that bi-Lagrangian subspaces always exist, so that LG( V, J ) is never empty. In general, this is a projective algebraic variety with rather non-trivial properties, which essentially depen d on the algebraic type of the pencil J. In particular, there might exists bi-Lagrangian subspaces of diffe rent algebraic types. In other words, LG( V, J ) may consist of several orbits of the automorphism group Aut( V, J ).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $V$ be a finite-dimensional vector space over $\mathbb{R}$ (or $\mathbb{C}$), and let $J = \{A_\lambda = A + \lambda B : \lambda \in \mathbb{P}^1\}$ be a pencil of skew-symmetric bilinear forms on $V$, where $A,B : V \times V \to \mathbb{F}$ are skew-symmetric. Define the automorphism group of the pencil by
$$\mathrm{Aut}(V,J) = \{ g \in GL(V) : g^*A = A \text{ and } g^*B = B \}.$$
The corank of the pencil is $\mathrm{corank}\, J := \min_{\lambda} \dim \ker A_\lambda$. A subspace $L \subset V$ is called bi-Lagrangian for $J$ if it is isotropic with respect to both $A$ and $B$ (i.e. $A(L,L) = B(L,L) = 0$) and has the maximal possible dimension
$$\dim L = \tfrac{1}{2}(\dim V + \mathrm{corank}\, J).$$
Let $LG(V,J)$ denote the set of all bi-Lagrangian subspaces of $V$; it is known to be a nonempty projective algebraic variety carrying a natural $\mathrm{Aut}(V,J)$-action.

(a) Describe the partition of $V$ into $\mathrm{Aut}(V,J)$-orbits.

(b) More generally, for each $1 \le k \le \dim V - 1$, describe the action of $\mathrm{Aut}(V,J)$ on the Grassmannian $\mathrm{Gr}_k(V)$ of $k$-dimensional subspaces of $V$: classify the orbits, find a complete system of invariants, and determine the fixed points (i.e. the $\mathrm{Aut}(V,J)$-invariant subspaces of $V$).

(c) Give a detailed description of the bi-Lagrangian Grassmannian $LG(V,J)$ as a projective algebraic variety, including its decomposition into $\mathrm{Aut}(V,J)$-orbits and the algebraic types of bi-Lagrangian subspaces it contains, in terms of the Jordan–Kronecker (algebraic) type of the pencil $J$.
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as an open research problem on the structure of the bi-Lagrangian Grassmannian of a Jordan–Kronecker pencil. No comprehensive classification appears to have been published; partial results exist in works of Bolsinov, Izosimov, and collaborators on Jordan–Kronecker invariants, but a full orbit/algebraic-type description of $LG(V,J)$ remains open.

status_evidence.title: Jordan–Kronecker invariants of finite-dimensional Lie algebras
status_evidence.snippet: Studies the algebraic type of pencils of skew-symmetric forms and related invariants, with classification of bi-Lagrangian-type subspaces remaining incomplete in general.
status_evidence.claim: Foundational results on pencils of skew forms exist, but a full description of bi-Lagrangian Grassmannians is not provided.
